Reading the Scoreboard

The scoreboard tells you who is strong, who is fed and whether your team should fight. Learn what to look for and when to check it.

Opening the scoreboard

Hold Tab (the default key) during a game to open the scoreboard. It lists all ten players, and for each one you can see their champion, level, kills, deaths and assists, CS, items and summoner spells. Release the key to close it.

The exact layout can change between patches, and you can change the key in your settings, but those basics are always there. Get used to opening it for a second or two at a time, a few times a minute when nothing is happening.

Who is strong? Compare items and levels

Kills don't tell you everything. The best way to judge strength is to compare items and levels.

  • Items: count completed items, not just item slots. A player with two finished items is much stronger than one with five small components. You can hover over an item to see what it is.
  • Levels: even one or two levels make a big difference early in the game. A higher level means more health and damage, and often a stronger ability rank. At level 6, most champions get their ultimate, so a level 6 player against a level 5 player has a huge advantage.
  • Kills and deaths: useful, but a player with few kills and lots of CS can be just as rich as one with many kills.
Pro tipCompare yourself with your lane opponent first. Same level and similar items? Trade carefully. You're ahead? Play forward. You're behind? Farm safely until you catch up.

Spot the fed enemy

A fed enemy is one who got many kills early and now has more items than anyone else. They're the biggest danger in every fight.

  • Avoid fighting them alone. If the fed enemy is a fighter or assassin, don't walk around the map by yourself where they could find you.
  • Build against them. If their damage is physical, armor helps; if it's magic, magic resist helps. See Items and Gold: How to Shop.
  • Decide who to focus. In a fight, it's often better to kill the squishiest enemy you can reach, and to keep the fed enemy busy with crowd control, than to dive into a fed tank.
  • Remember the bounty. Players who get a lot of kills carry a bounty, so killing them gives extra gold. A careful team fight around the fed enemy can turn the game.
Common mistakeLooking only at your own lane. The fed enemy might be in another lane and on their way to you. Check the whole scoreboard, not just your opponent.

Summoner spells and cooldowns

The scoreboard shows which summoner spells each enemy took. Knowing that an enemy has Flash and Ghost, or Teleport, tells you how they'll escape or join fights.

If you or your team have been noting enemy cooldowns (for example, typing "mid flash" with the time in chat), check those notes before you fight. Flash has a 5-minute cooldown, so an enemy without Flash is much easier to catch for a while. Many players also ping summoner cooldowns from the scoreboard so the whole team knows. See Summoner Spells and Runes for more on summoner spells.

Using CS and level gaps to decide whether to fight

Before a fight or objective, take a quick look at both teams:

  • Is your team behind on levels? If most of your team is one or two levels lower, avoid even fights. Farm, defend near your towers, and wait for the enemy to make a mistake.
  • Is the CS gap big? About 15 to 20 CS is worth roughly as much gold as a kill. A laner who is 40 CS ahead is richer than their kill count shows.
  • Is a key enemy about to finish an item? If they're close to completing a big item, it can be worth fighting before they recall and buy it. If they just bought it, wait for your own spike. See Power Spikes: Know When You're Strong.

None of this has to be exact. You're just asking: "Are we stronger, even, or weaker right now?" That answer should guide whether you take the fight or back off.

When to look, and when not to

The scoreboard covers a large part of your screen, so timing matters.

  • Good times: while you're dead, while walking back to lane, right after you recall, when the wave is far away, and before a dragon or Baron fight.
  • Bad times: in the middle of a fight, while dodging spells, or when an enemy is near you. A second of not seeing the fight can cost you your life.

If you check the scoreboard before the fight starts, you already know who to watch out for when it begins.

Key takeaways

  • Hold Tab (by default) to see every player's level, KDA, CS, items and summoner spells.
  • Judge strength by completed items and levels, not just kills.
  • Find the fed enemy, avoid fighting them alone, and build against their damage.
  • If your team is behind on levels or items, avoid even fights and wait.
  • Check the scoreboard during quiet moments, never in the middle of a fight.
